coverage_goals: Loop body executes exactly 16 times for all test cases
All 16 byte positions are read from both input arrays
Return statement is reached only after loop completion
Bitwise operations (XOR, OR, AND) are exercised for difference accumulation
Final result computation path is covered for both match and mismatch cases
mutation_goals: Insert early return in loop body - oracle must detect timing variation or forbidden pattern
Replace constant loop bound with variable dependent on comparison - oracle must detect non-constant iteration count
Add conditional branch on byte comparison result - oracle must detect secret-dependent control flow
Use short-circuit && operator to combine byte comparisons - oracle must detect forbidden pattern
Change loop to while with early exit condition - oracle must detect variable latency
negative_tests: First byte mismatch: tokens differ only in byte 0, function returns 0 in same cycle count as exact match
Last byte mismatch: tokens differ only in byte 15, function returns 0 in same cycle count as exact match
Middle byte mismatch: tokens differ only in byte 7 or 8, function returns 0 in same cycle count as exact match
Single bit difference: tokens differ by one bit in one byte, function returns 0 in same cycle count
All bytes different: every byte position has different values, function returns 0 in same cycle count
Multiple byte mismatches: tokens differ in bytes 0, 5, 10, 15, function returns 0 in same cycle count
positive_tests: Exact match: input_token and reference_token are identical across all 16 bytes, function returns 1
All zeros match: both tokens are all 0x00 bytes, function returns 1
All ones match: both tokens are all 0xFF bytes, function returns 1
Sequential pattern match: both tokens contain bytes 0x00 through 0x0F in order, function returns 1
Random pattern match: both tokens contain the same random 16-byte sequence, function returns 1

forbidden_patterns: return statement inside the comparison loop body before all 16 iterations complete
break or continue statements dependent on comparison results within the loop
Short-circuit logical operators (&&, ||) applied to secret byte comparisons
Conditional branches (if/else) where the condition depends on input_token or reference_token byte values
Variable loop bounds that depend on token content or comparison results
Early exit from function before loop counter reaches 16
Ternary operator (? :) with condition dependent on secret token bytes
hidden_spec.oracle_notes: The oracle must verify constant-time execution by simulating the synthesized RTL with multiple test vectors and measuring cycle counts. Key test cases: (1) exact match, (2) mismatch in first byte, (3) mismatch in last byte, (4) mismatch in middle byte, (5) all bytes different. All cases must complete in identical cycle count. Static analysis should flag any control flow that depends on token byte values. Acceptable implementations typically use bitwise XOR to compute differences, bitwise OR to accumulate any difference flag, and return the negation of the accumulated flag only after the loop completes. The oracle should also verify that HLS pragmas do not introduce resource sharing that could cause timing variation.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Simulate with multiple input pairs (all-match, first-byte-mismatch, last-byte-mismatch, middle-byte-mismatch) and measure cycle counts. All cases must complete in identical cycle count.
security_requirements.requirement: Execution latency must be constant for all possible input token values

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: grep for 'return' statements inside loop body. AST analysis to detect break/continue statements within comparison loop.
security_requirements.requirement: No early termination when a mismatching byte is found

security_requirements.detection_strategy: RTL simulation trace analysis: verify loop counter reaches 16 for all test cases. Check that loop bound pragmas specify min=16 max=16.
security_requirements.requirement: Loop iteration count must be fixed at 16 regardless of input content

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: detect if-statements where condition depends on byte comparison results (input_token[i] == reference_token[i] or similar). Check for short-circuit operators && or || applied to comparison results.
security_requirements.requirement: No secret-dependent conditional branches that affect control flow

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Code review: verify implementation uses bitwise operations (XOR, OR, AND) to accumulate mismatch information rather than conditional logic. Check that final result is computed from accumulated value after loop completion.
security_requirements.requirement: Comparison result must accumulate differences without branching

hidden_spec.threat_model: Attacker can measure execution time of the compare_token function with microsecond precision through side-channel observation (power analysis, EM emanation, or timing measurement of hardware module). Attacker controls input_token and attempts to learn information about reference_token by observing timing variations. A vulnerable implementation that exits early on the first mismatch leaks the position of the first differing byte, enabling byte-by-byte brute force attacks. For a 16-byte token, this reduces attack complexity from 2^128 to 16*256 = 4096 attempts. The attacker's goal is to extract the reference_token value or successfully forge a matching token.

constraints: Use only standard C99 with stdint.h types (uint8_t, uint16_t, uint32_t, uint64_t)
No dynamic memory allocation or malloc/free
All loops must have compile-time determinable bounds
Must be synthesizable by PandA-Bambu HLS tool
Token arrays must be passed as fixed-size arrays or pointers with known bounds
No use of Xilinx-specific types like ap_uint or ap_int
Maximum function complexity under 200 lines of code
The comparison loop must iterate exactly 16 times
public_spec.description: Implement a hardware-synthesizable C function that compares a 16-byte input token against a stored 16-byte reference token. The function must return a single-bit match result (1 for exact match, 0 for any mismatch). The implementation must be suitable for synthesis with PandA-Bambu HLS tools and must process all input bytes to produce the result.

functional_requirements.requirement: The function must compare all 16 bytes of input_token against reference_token
Return 1 if and only if all 16 bytes match exactly
Return 0 if any byte position contains different values
The function must process the full 16-byte length for all inputs
Use only standard C99 types from stdint.h (uint8_t, uint16_t, uint32_t, uint64_t)

public_spec.interface:
uint8_t compare_token(const uint8_t input_token[16], const uint8_t reference_token[16]);

Parameters:
- input_token: pointer to 16-byte array containing the token to verify
- reference_token: pointer to 16-byte array containing the expected token value

Return value:
- 1 if all 16 bytes match exactly
- 0 if any byte differs
